nodes.text: for the poor thing came as if to cross over.
Plato
I throw the apple at you; and you, if you love me willingly,
take it and give me a share of your maidenhood;
but if your thoughts are what I pray they are not, take this same [apple]
and consider how short-lived youth’s bloom is.
Plato
I am an apple; someone who loves you throws me. Come, nod yes,
Xanthippe; both you and I are wasting away.
Dionysius the Sophist
You with the roses, you have a rosy charm; but what are you selling,
will sail from above, having climbed aboard an old woman’s twenty-oared hulk.
Anonymous
The *iynx* [magic wheel] of Nico, which knows how to draw a man even from across the sea
and boys out of their bedrooms,
decorated with gold, from translucent amethyst
carved, lies dedicated to you, Cypris, a cherished possession,
tied round the middle with the soft wool of a purple lamb,
the guest-gift of the Larissaean sorceress.
Leonidas
Melo and Satyra, of great age, Antigeneides’
